title: Raising admission to fifty cents and a dollar
summary: Recollections of the price going up, enforcing it at the door, and a story of a band returning to find they had to pay.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Yeah. And so, you know, you would, a lot of people would get approached, you know, so many times, you know, and other people, you know, wouldn't, and, you know, it was sort of unfair. So, you know, it was always, you know, sort of, I felt bad, you know, walking in front of the band and asking for money. But anyway, and then, but at some point it went to fifty cents. And then a few, I don't know, a few years later it went to a dollar, which is this now. It went, you probably don't remember the dates. Yeah, I do remember when I went to a dollar.
So we went to a dollar? We went away.

Everything that happened happened, you know, because it had to happen. Like, I couldn't get inside to collect people and come to, you know, stand at the inner carriage or at the door. I couldn't get inside at all. So I had to start asking people to make a donation. But, you know, we went away when somebody started asking for the keys that we made a donation, too. We went, was it Jack, was it Jack Beach? Yeah, he wouldn't like to go out on the city or something, he wouldn't like to go out on the city or something.
Oh yeah. I heard, you're the photographer. No, no, Jack.
Oh, John Beecher? No, B.J. and Jack. Yeah, Peers.

Peers, Jack Peers. Yes. Our next door neighbor, when we were living here, somebody from Philadelphia. He came over one night and said, this is no way to run a business. He took the thing. Well, first of all, he was six foot six, you know. I'd stand there, you know, just not let people in. We're out. I don't remember when we went to fifty cent minimum. But the dollar, I think it was the dollar, we went to, we left three ladies here watching the whole night. June Conn and two of her girlfriends, they're all lawyers. You probably know them. They're all, you know, they had that office, they had an office together. They were all getting it. And I don't know if we went out to play. We took a band, was the one we went to Boston.

Well, I knew when we looked, Dr. Orstin went back a bit. It was when they took us to Function Society, we went out with working with little angels. And we came home. And we walked into the door and one of the ladies wouldn't let me in because they were going to pay a dollar. And I was going to get down the two and grabbed my horn and said, hey, you know, please put a dollar in here if you want to come inside.
